title: Thermal vorticity and global equilibrium obstructions

items.title: Thermal vorticity and equilibrium domain
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a nonempty connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with its Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ and length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. Let $\beta$ be a smooth future-directed timelike Killing vector field on $O$, with components in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, and fix $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K}^{-1}$. On $O$ define

$$T:=\frac{1}{k_B\sqrt{-g(\beta,\beta)}},\qquad u:=k_BT\,\beta,\qquad \varpi_{ab}:=-\frac12(\nabla_a\beta_b-\nabla_b\beta_a).$$

Thus $T$ is in kelvins, $g(u,u)=-1$, and the covariant two-form $\varpi$ has units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, set $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ and $\alpha:=-\zeta$, both dimensionless. These fields are defined only on the region where $\beta$ is future timelike; no thermal state or material realization is part of this definition.

references.title: F. Becattini, Thermodynamic equilibrium in relativity: four-temperature, Killing vectors and Lie derivatives, §§3–5, eqs. (6), (11)–(16)
Jessica Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§III–IV, eqs. (4.1)–(4.6)
David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.4.1–2.4.5 and §4.3.1

items.title: Period of a smooth one-form along a closed curve
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold, meaning a topological $n$-manifold equipped with a maximal smooth atlas, and let $\omega\in\Omega^1(M)$ be a smooth real one-form, meaning a smooth section of the cotangent bundle $T^*M\to M$. Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ be a continuous piecewise-$C^1$ curve with $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)$: there is a finite subdivision $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1$ such that on each closed piece a chart contains the curve image, its coordinate representative is $C^1$ on the piece interior, and its derivative extends continuously to the endpoints. At a piece endpoint, use the corresponding one-sided derivative as the tangent. On each piece, pair this tangent $\dot\gamma(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ with $\omega_{\gamma(t)}\in T^*_{\gamma(t)}M$. Define the oriented period by

$$\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega):=\sum_j\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))\,dt,$$

where $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1$ is any admissible chartwise subdivision with the regularity specified above. The covector-vector pairing is intrinsic, and additivity makes this value independent of further subdivision. No invariance under homotopy is asserted by this definition.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.3.1 and 2.4.1–2.4.5

items.title: A global potential compensator makes the contracted field exact
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian domain, let $\xi$ be a smooth future-timelike Killing field on $O$, and let $A$ be a global smooth one-form with $F=dA$. Suppose a global smooth scalar $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfies $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define $\Psi_\xi:=\xi^aA_a-\Lambda_\xi$ and $\omega:=\iota_\xi F$, with $(\iota_\xi F)_a=\xi^bF_{ba}$. Then

$$\omega=-d\Psi_\xi,$$

so $\omega$ is exact. This identity uses the global potential symmetry and assumes no charged trajectory or conservation law.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.B, eqs. (262)-(268)
David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §2.4.4

items.title: An exact one-form has zero period on every closed piecewise-C¹ curve
items.statement: On any smooth manifold $M$, if a smooth one-form $\omega$ is exact, so $\omega=d\phi$ for a globally defined smooth scalar $\phi:M\to\mathbb R$, then $\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega)=0$ for every closed piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma$ in $M$.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.4.3–2.4.5

The components of $\omega$ have units $\mathrm{T\,J}^{-1}$. Assume $d\omega=0$. Here exact means $\omega=d\psi$ for a globally defined smooth scalar $\psi$ with units $\mathrm{T\,m\,J}^{-1}$; for a piecewise-$C^1$ closed curve $\gamma:[0,1]	o O$, its period is the oriented integral $\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega):=\sum_j\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))\,dt$, with the curve regularity and endpoint convention in the period definition. Let $m>0$ be a particle rest mass in kilograms, let $q_{m SI}
e0$ be a constant charge in coulombs, and take $c>0$ in metres per second. Set $q_{m eff}:=cq_{m SI}$, with units $\mathrm{C\,m\,s}^{-1}$. Choose any constant $T_*>0$ kelvins and put $\xi:=k_BT_* eta$ and $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$. Then $\xi$ is a future-timelike Killing field with dimensionless components, $u=\xi/N_\xi$ is future unit timelike, $N_\xi=T_*/T$, and $ eta=u/(k_BT)$. These are the stationary geometric data required by the charged stationarity theorem. For the ansatz $f=\exp(\zeta+g( eta,P))$ on the future massive shell defined by the charged particle data, with $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ and $\alpha:=-\zeta$, stationarity is equivalent, in this already-Killing subcase, to $d\alpha=q_{m eff}\omega$; both sides have inverse-length units. Thus the equation for an unknown global smooth dimensionless scalar $\alpha$ has a solution exactly when $\omega$ is exact; any nonzero period obstructs such a solution. The scalar $\alpha$ corresponds to chemical potential $\mu=-k_BT\alpha$ in joules.

If the same normalized field $\xi=k_BT_* eta$ has a global potential compensator $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$, then $\omega$ is exact and all its periods vanish. For the rotating model, take global Cartesian length coordinates $(x^0,x,y,z)$ on Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^4$, with $x^0=ct$, metric $-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, and future direction selected by $\partial_{x^0}$. Put $r:=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and, away from the axis $r=0$, let $\phi$ be the polar angle in the $x,y$-plane. The rotation field $\partial_\phi:=-y\partial_x+x\partial_y$ is defined by this Cartesian formula on all of $M$, including the axis; away from the axis the metric is $-(dx^0)^2+dr^2+r^2d\phi^2+dz^2$. For $b>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $\Omega\in\mathbb R$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, set $ eta:=b(\partial_{x^0}+\Omega\partial_\phi)$. This field is future timelike exactly where $1-\Omega^2r^2>0$. When $\Omega
e0$ this is $r<1/|\Omega|$ and $T=1/(k_Bb\sqrt{1-\Omega^2r^2})$; when $\Omega=0$ every $r$ is allowed and $T=1/(k_Bb)$. These rotating formulas use the same SI length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ as the preceding clauses; no natural-unit substitution is made.

title: Thermal vorticity and global equilibrium obstructions — Examples

items.title: Rigid bath and nonexact electric period
items.statement:
Use global Cartesian length coordinates $(x^0,x,y,z)$ on Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^4$, with $x^0=ct$, metric $-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, and future direction selected by $\partial_{x^0}$. Set $r:=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and let $\phi$ be the polar angle away from $r=0$; the rotation field $\partial_\phi:=-y\partial_x+x\partial_y$ is defined smoothly on all of $M$ by its Cartesian expression. Let

$$O:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:\tfrac14\,\mathrm m<\sqrt{x^2+y^2}<\tfrac34\,\mathrm m\}\times\mathbb R_z,$$

so the spatial section is an annulus and all fields below are defined on this four-dimensional product domain. Adopt the exact SI defining values $k_B=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K}^{-1}$ and $c=299792458\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$. For $b=1\,\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, $\Omega=1\,\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, and $r=\tfrac12\,\mathrm m$, the rotating field $\beta=b(\partial_{x^0}+\Omega\partial_\phi)$ has $T=2\,\mathrm J/(\sqrt3 k_B)$. Define the smooth one-form $\eta:=(-y\,dx+x\,dy)/(x^2+y^2)$ on $O$, set $A:=C_0x^0\eta$ and $F:=dA=C_0\,dx^0\wedge\eta$ for a fixed nonzero $C_0$ in $\mathrm{T\,m}$. For any fixed nonzero SI charge $q_{\rm SI}$ in coulombs, define $q_{\rm eff}:=cq_{\rm SI}\ne0$ in $\mathrm{C\,m\,s}^{-1}$. Then $\omega:=\iota_\beta F=bC_0(\eta-\Omega dx^0)$ is closed and has period $2\pi bC_0\ne0$ on every positively oriented circle of fixed $x^0,z,r$ in the spatial annulus. Hence no global smooth dimensionless scalar $\alpha:O\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $d\alpha=q_{\rm eff}\omega$.
